## 0.21.0 — 2026-11-20
- Follow up on a line. Type `>mon`, `>tomorrow`, `>+3d`, `>2w` or `>next week` at the end of a task, commitment or decision and press space or Enter: it turns into a date (`>2026-11-23`) written in the line. A chip in the right rail shows it ("Mon 23 Nov · in 3 days", red when late); hover any open item for "Follow up" and a picker: Tomorrow, Monday, Next week, In 2 weeks, a date, or none.
- Review ▸ Revisit now starts with "Lines to follow up" from every note: Overdue, Today, This week, Later. Tick one done, snooze it to Tomorrow or Monday, pick a day, or open it.
- Notes already had a follow-up flag; it now has a Monday button too.
- The AI helper's `list_open_actions` returns each line's `follow_up` date and takes `due_by` and `has_follow_up` (needs the sync server update). Desktop only for the picker; the phone keeps the dates in the text.

## 0.20.0 — 2026-11-20
- The AI helper (MCP) tools are richer, from a helper's feedback. Lists sort by when the session happened, take date ranges and page, and every result carries tags, people (attendees and @mentions merged), namespace, intent, open task and commitment counts and word count, with ISO dates. New `list_open_actions` (every unchecked `[]` and `![]` with its note, day and line) and `get_sessions`. Search takes "quoted phrases", `-excluded`, `tag:`, `person:` and `ns:`, and ranks title matches first. The tool descriptions explain the markers and intent values.
- The instructions you paste into a helper list the new tools. Needs the sync server update; until it is deployed the old three tools keep working.

## 0.19.0 — 2026-11-20
- Soft pull-in. If a line in another note links to this page with `[[This page]]`, that line (with the lines indented under it) now shows under this page in a "Pulled in" section, grouped by note. The text stays written in the source note: nothing is copied or stored, so it is always current.
- Tick a pulled task and it ticks in the source note. "Open source" jumps to the line. "Move here" takes it off the original page for good: the line moves into this page and leaves a `↳` stub behind.
- The first three notes show open, the rest behind "Show more". The right rail shows the count and jumps to the section. The Inbox, Scratch notes and notes in another workspace are left out. A `hub/note` title is not a link. Desktop only.

## 0.18.0 — 2026-11-20
- Undo and redo for the text of a note: ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z (or ⌘Y), the ↶ ↷ buttons by the save status, the Edit menu, and ⌘K "Undo" / "Redo". It covers typing (grouped by pause), ticking a task, changing a line's marker, moving lines, groups, and everything in a focus thread, including sorting and removing it.
- Each note keeps its own history while the app is open. It starts fresh when the note is changed from outside (sync, or a capture filed into it), so an undo never wipes that. Titles, type and other fields keep the text box's own undo. Desktop only.

## 0.17.0 — 2026-11-20
- Focus a line now expands in place. The thread card opens right under its line, inside the note, and the lines below move down to make room. It grows as you type. Esc or ⌘⇧↵ closes it and the lines close up again.
- To make room, the editor holds a few invisible blank lines under the focused line while the thread is open. They are never saved, copied or synced.

## 0.16.0 — 2026-11-20
- Hubs. A note titled `pricing/tiers` is in the hub `pricing`: no field, no filing step. Link with `[[pricing/tiers]]`. One level only (the first slash splits).
- The sidebar now has a Hubs section with a count each, and hub notes leave the Recent list (search, ⌘K and links still reach them). Open a hub note and its hub is highlighted.
- A hub page has three tabs. Notes: every note in the hub, plus open tasks and commitments, decisions, questions, people and topics from all of them. Timeline: the same scrolling timeline, only for this hub. Relationships: links inside the hub, out of it and into it from other notes, and which people show up across the notes.
- On a hub page: New note (starts as `hub/`), Write about this hub (a note titled just the hub name, shown at the top), and Rename, which rewrites every `hub/…` title and `[[hub/…]]` link after you confirm the counts.
- Hubs follow the workspace you are viewing. URLs at the start of a note, and titles like `and/`, are not hubs. The phone still lists every note (hubs are desktop only for now).
- ⌘K: "Open hub …".

## 0.15.0 — 2026-11-20
- Snippets: type `/` at the start of a line to see them (`/template` or any part of a name filters). Built in: /standup, /meeting, /1on1, /decision, /retro, /date, /time. Enter inserts it and puts the cursor in the first blank spot. {{date}}, {{time}}, {{day}} and {{title}} fill in.
- Your own templates are ordinary notes titled "Template: Name". Make one with ⌘K → "Save this note as a template", or select text and choose "Save the selected text as a template". Then `/name` inserts it.
- Emoji, Slack style: type `:smi` to pick from a list, or finish `:tada:` and it turns into 🎉. The emoji is written into the text, so notes stay plain text. Desktop only.

## 0.14.2 — 2026-11-20
- Making an AI helper token now also shows ready-to-paste instructions for the helper: the server address, the auth header with the token, and the three tools. A Copy instructions button copies them. Shown once, like the token.
